utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's bring the accused in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin is in. Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is the Case Number IT-99-36-T, The Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please take a seat. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, Julian Nicholls, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Ms. Korner, and to your colleagues. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. David Cunningham with Aleksandar Vujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Cunningham and Mr. Vujic. My apologies on behalf of the Trial Chamber for starting late. Something happened, and we just couldn't start earlier. My apologies again. Preliminaries? So could we have the witness in, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Dejanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome once more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed straight away with the cross-examination, which we started yesterday. May I just remind you that -- of the solemn declaration that you made yesterday. That applies also for today. Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Korner: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dejanovic, I want to ask you one further question in relation to Mr. Brdjanin. You told Mr. Cunningham yesterday that Mr. Brdjanin was not a powerful man. He was a man without power. Do you still wish to adhere to that answer, stick to that answer?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [In English] Yes, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was, during the relevant period, was he not, that is between, say, August of 1991 and the end of 1992, first of all a deputy to the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, still it doesn't meaning that he was a powerful man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you agree he was a deputy?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that he was the vice-president, first of all, of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. Probably he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that he became the president of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that he subsequently became a minister in the government of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think later on, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a vice-president of the government of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was vice-president later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And despite all those positions that he held during that period, in your view, he was a man of no importance and no influence. Is that what you're telling the Court?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say that at that time, the real power, considering all bad things, all enemies on the ground -- [Interpretation] Not enemy, but hostilities, the real power was not on that position which he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think it may be better for you, Mr. Dejanovic, and perhaps for all of us if you speak in your own language and have the translation. I don't quite understand what you mean by this. Where -- you say he had no real power. Where do you say the real power was?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I have to apologise, but I'm receiving interpretation in my own language, and that is kind of confusing for me, so I would like to continue in my own language. I think I can state that the real power, bearing in mind the state of war that existed in the actual -- on the ground was not in the hands of the civilian authorities and in the positions that Mr. Brdjanin held and that you just enumerated. I don't know whether now I've made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say it was not in the hands of the civilian authorities. In whose hands do you say that power was?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's quite clear. Well, it depends on what we are talking about. If we talk about military issues, the power was in the hands of the military structures. If we talk about other aspects, other things, for instance, the police, they had their own chain of command, their own authorities. So did the military, and the civilian authorities had their jurisdiction over civilian matters. Mr. Brdjanin as a minister, if I remember correctly, was in charge of urban planning and construction, if I'm not mistaken. So that would his sphere of competence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dejanovic, you're not suggesting, are you, that the military and the police acted without orders from the civilian authorities? That was not a military dictatorship in the Republika Srpska, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not a military dictatorship, but the military had its own chain of command, its own hierarchy that it used in its actions. Let me just clarify this: The government that we recognised at that time, well, in fact, you discussed broader time period, and I will try to make my answer relevant to the entire period. The government that we recognised was the one of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina which had its own structures and organs which functioned in a way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. The power was still the civilian power at Republic, I suggest, regional, and municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you say "power." Everybody had their own sphere of responsibility, and the government structures existed at all levels. There was the government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there was the association, the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to spend too long on this because there are many other matters that I have to deal with today. But the fact is, is it, that the policies and in particular the policy of what you will call neutrally separation from the other nationalities in Bosnia was one devised by the politicians, the civilian authorities, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand your question. I understood it in terms of language, but I fail to grasp the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go around it in another manner. You have agreed already that at the time it was not a military dictatorship.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, would you agree also that it was not a police dictatorship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically, it was a government structure where you have the civilian authorities, the police authorities, the military authorities functioning together in a time of crisis, in a time of war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree with this statement. But I have to emphasise that there was a war going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I mentioned that myself. The police had its own chain of command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the highest level of that command, the chief of police, number one, absolute number one, was he answerable to anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The minister of the interior was responsible to the government, and the government was responsible to the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are getting there. The highest member of the army in the chain of command, was he answerable to anyone? Who was the chief of staff at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember. I believe that was Mr. Mladic was the chief of command, the Main Staff. But at the time when the time now I'm testifying about, when the JNA still existed our political --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, forget about the JNA. We are talking of a later phase now. And who was the commander in chief?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, it was Mr. Mladic at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, the commander in chief. For example, the commander in chief in the former Yugoslavia, the whole country when it was still unified, who was the commander in chief?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the presidency of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And of Republika Srpska, who was the commander in chief of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the Army of Republika Srpska was established, the presidency of Republika Srpska was the commander in chief of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the presidency of Republika Srpska was a civilian authority? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So ultimately at the head, you always have the civilian authority, which controls the destiny of the country, be it war or no state of war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move on from this topic now. Now, you told us yesterday that in your view the association of Bosnian Krajina municipalities, ZOBK, was a voluntary organisation, and so was the Assembly of the Autonomous Region. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I think we have two questions here. The association itself was a voluntary organisation. The assembly was just an organ. I cannot say whether that was a voluntary or involuntary organisation. It was an organ that was set up in accordance with an agreement that was reached about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't it strike you as odd when you read the statute of the association of Bosnian Krajina municipalities, an economic association, that it contained provisions about defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there is a provision in the statute of the association of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina. This is not something unusual in our context. Every municipality has a similar provision. Even a company would have the same provision in its statute at that time, that it should take care of issues related to the coordination of the defence and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is no, it didn't strike you as odd?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not odd at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in September 1991, the assembly of the association turned itself into the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in the Assembly of the Serbian People held on the 21st of November, after the plebiscite, the autonomous regions in what was declared to be the Serbian Republic were verified, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact definition. It was said that the autonomous regions would make part of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So they became part of it. But I do not recall the exact wording.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'll put it to you, because we've seen the document a number of times - I'm referring to P50 - decisions -- sorry, P17. "Decisions on the proclamation of the Serbian autonomous regions in Bosnia and Herzegovina are hereby verified." That was the actual wording. Your municipality, Bosanski Novi, was one of the municipalities that formed the autonomous region. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, we joined the autonomous region. I don't know whether this is an important distinction. We were not in the first group that set up the association. We joined it at a later stage. I don't know whether that's important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that exactly. You didn't apparently manage to join formally until time in May 1992. But in actual fact, you were listed by the government, the Serbian Government, as one of the municipalities that made up the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from that period, up until the abolition of the regional level in September of 1992, the regional authorities formed part, didn't they, of the governmental authorities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did it in accordance with their statute. I think it's an important issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand what I'm trying to do? I'm suggesting to you, sir, that contrary to what you asserted yesterday, that the regional authorities in the form of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region, and later its crisis staff, had real authority and power.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to reiterate: Despite the fact that the autonomous regions had become part of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, their statute, as it was, remained in force. This statute stipulated that any decisions made by the Autonomous Region of Krajina must be ratified by the local authorities. This, in effect, means that such an organ did not have a de facto executive power. I wanted to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You see, you also told us yesterday, and I suggest that is because that you and Mr. Vidic discussed this together, that the ARK -- the Autonomous Region Assembly had -- let me find the exact words for a moment, you used. This is at page 29 of LiveNote. The meetings that you attended were like Hyde Park. I take it you mean by that Speakers Corner where everybody can speak in Hyde Park. Is that what you were referring to? "Everyone can enter. Everyone can have a speech. Everyone can go in and out as they want." And so on. It was a very unserious job. And you repeated that. And then you said you were asked: As a result of your conclusion, what was your perception of the ARK Assembly's power or its competence? No, it was not competent. Now, did you attend the meeting of the assembly on the 29th of February when Mr. Karadzic came down? Just let me read you the rest of the people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not going to bother to get the exhibit out because we have been over it a number of times. I'll find my own copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, Mr. Koljevic, Mr. Ostojic, and others. Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that I attended it. If I may, as regards the possible links with the statement by Mr. Vidic, I have to say that I used the phrase "Hyde Park," and I described the situation in this way, I did it the first time when I met with Mr. Cunningham a month ago. So please do not try to make any connection between what I originally said, the way that I compared the situation with Hyde Park with anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Mr. Vidic spoke at -- at least one of these assemblies?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one of the sessions of the Autonomous Region of Krajina? Is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I've already stated that I attended very few of these sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you still maintain that this was an assembly without authority or power or importance?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was an assembly that did not have executive power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've already told us and confirmed at the end of yesterday that you never, ever implemented any decisions made either by the assembly or by the crisis staff of the region. I'd like you now, please, to have a look at Exhibit P2547. Do you recognise the Official Gazette of the Bosanski Novi Municipality dated the 10th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's an error in the date on the top. If you look at the original, it clearly says 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Or it has been translated as 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document, Mr. Dejanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that this is the Official Gazette of the Bosanski Novi Municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I would like you -- the first decision, Article 1, is to apply the regulations of the old Yugoslavia effectively until the Serbian Republic has passed various laws. Could you go, please, however, to the second decision which says: "Pursuant to Article 86..." Decision, Article 1: "The Bosanski Novi SDK Office shall be detached from the Sarajevo SDK Head Office, Prijedor branch, and the decision on the Autonomous Region of Krajina public auditing service issued at the ARK Assembly session of the 4th of March 1992 shall be adopted whereby an SDK Office will be opened as part of the Bosanska Gradiska SDK branch..." et cetera. Presumably, you were well aware of this decision because you were running the SDK.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was appointed the head of the SDK later. But I was familiar with the decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain why, if the assembly as it still was in April of the autonomous region had no authority, you should do this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I didn't say that we did not implement any of the decisions. I want to say that the economic issues were of paramount importance for the autonomous region. But by this decision, the assembly confirmed what it wanted to achieve. One of the economic solutions that was in our interest to implement was implemented in the manner described herein. I stated quite clearly that all the decisions had to be ratified by the assemblies at the municipal level. Municipalities that made part of the autonomous region. So this is exactly what happened. The assembly ratified one of the decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I can assure you, sir, you told us that you didn't adopt any of the decisions yesterday. But we'll move on. Now, the reason -- thank you. You can hand that document back.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to apologise. Perhaps I did make a mistake. But I really did not want to say that none of the decisions had been implemented. There was the statute of the autonomous region. And according to the statute, some of the decisions that were in our favour had to be ratified by the municipal assemblies that wanted to have it implemented. And this decision speaks in favour of this statement of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm going to show you some other decisions which you may have forgotten about. The reason why the Bosniaks in Bosanski Novi didn't want Bosanski Novi to join the Autonomous Region Assembly or any other kind of organisation was because it was clear, wasn't it, to you, that it was nothing more than a body designed to coordinate the Serb -- the Bosnian Serb efforts to separate from the other nationalities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot go into attempts to clarify the reasons which prompted Bosniaks to do something or not do something. They could do that themselves. We had our own reasons. We had our legitimate political wishes to preserve Yugoslavia. When this failed, I believe that we still had the legitimate reason to set up this assembly which would negotiate a settlement. And I know that at one point that we never wanted this territory or this state to be cleansed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's not what the Muslims themselves thought privately; it's what they said to you, wasn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were in constant contact with them, and we did discuss things. Probably, I can only assume, that they probably feared that this was a political solution. The Autonomous Region of Krajina was something that was leading to a political solution which was not in their favour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't -- you can't -- it's not that you assume it. They actually said that, didn't they? They said, and in particular, the president of the SDA, Mr. Muhamed - I have always had problems with this name, Muhamedagic, he said in terms didn't he that they didn't want to join because this was a Serb organisation which was going to be, as it were, used as a coordinating body against the Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that those are his words. I cannot recall at this point. It's his right to form opinions, as was ours, as regards this particular organisation. [In English] I'm sorry. [Interpretation] Sorry, are you talking about Izet Muhamedagic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is supposedly -- the same person that supposedly together with whom they collected the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed in a helicopter crash sometime later on, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the Bosanski Novi SDS declined, didn't they, to make any provision for the referendum that was to be held in -- was held in February of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina we believed -- or rather, it was said that Serbs were constituent peoples. Serb deputies in the assembly having expressed their wish believed this referendum to be directly against Serbs, and this is the reasons why we didn't wish to take part in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not only did you not take part, you didn't give any assistance at all for the holding of the referendum?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The referendum in question as far as we were concerned was an illegal one, so we took no part whatsoever in organising it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was after that referendum, wasn't it, that the tensions really began to rise in Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I can agree with you. Not only because of the referendum. I already explained that the town of Bosanski Novi was in a very special situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that the crisis staff of the autonomous region had -- I'm sorry. You told us -- there, you were quite definite that you never saw -- you were shown the Gazette decisions. You never saw any of them, and you didn't do anything about them. Do you remember saying that yesterday? Page 58 of the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that this is what I said. And once again, I didn't see any of the Official Gazettes. The reasons, perhaps, having to do with the nature of my work, I didn't come across any of them. I never saw any of them. I mean, this was not legislation which guided our activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you have a look, please, at Exhibit P186. That's a decision addressed from the crisis staff to the president of the municipal assembly. "Pursuant to the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of the 11th of May 1992, we submit to you the statements of accounts for financing of institutions and the defence of the autonomous region. Could you please immediately deposit the set amounts to transfer account number..." et cetera. If we look under Bosanski Novi, 4, population times 30 dinars per head, 1.246.230 dinars. Now, could you have a look, please, at P2539. Four days later on the 15th of May, the executive committee of the assembly stated that "on the basis of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina telex of the 11th of May - and it gives the number, and we can see that number if we look at the previous document - issued the following: The Bosanski Novi municipal administration secretariat is ordered to pay 1.246.230 dinars into the account of the Autonomous Region of Krajina institutions. The order comes into effect immediately." Is that something you had forgotten about, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall this decision either. It is possible that there are more of such decisions or orders. But I don't think that it shows that all decisions were automatically implemented. We have an organ, a body here which adopted a decision to a certain effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why would you do this, sir, if in your view this is a - I'm paraphrasing - a hopelessly inefficient, powerless organisation? Why give them all this money?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why the executive committee did this. It was certainly contrary to the statute of the municipal assembly and the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the reason, I suggest to you, sir, and you know full well it was done is because during this period of time, the crisis staff of the region had authority. That's the reality, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that. There could have been some individual cases like that, but municipal organs had to function pursuant to statutory provisions. This is an example of a violation of the statute of the municipal assembly and the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm going to stop you here because you're not answering the question. Ms. Korner asked you, "Well, the reason I suggest to you, sir, you know full well it was done is because during this period of time the crisis staff of the region had authority. That's the reality, isn't it, sir?" Now, you are giving an answer which may be correct insofar as the municipality is concerned, but you are not answering her question. You said I wouldn't agree with that. "There could have been some individual cases like that, but municipal organs had to function pursuant to statutory provisions. This is an example of a violation of the statute of the municipal assembly and the Autonomous Region of Krajina." But you've still not commented or answered on the suggestion that was put to you by Ms. Korner; namely, that all this, including violations of the statute of the municipal assembly was done precisely because the crisis staff of the ARK had authority?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I'm going to object to your question because I believed with his answer "I wouldn't agree with that" that he answers the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But he is answering a question without giving an explanation, and he tries to give an explanation which does not tally at all with the reason why he is not agreeing with the question that was put to him by Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Then he should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If the municipality decides to take steps which are in accordance with his opinion a violation of the statute of the municipal assembly, it certainly does not explain his stand or his opinion that the crisis staff of the ARK was not important and was almost a ridiculous organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: He answered the question that was put to him. Now he's being criticised because he didn't give an explanation. If he's asked to give an explanation, he'll do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He was asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When you admonish the witnesses every day, you say be as precise and concise with his questions, and I do that in my proofing sessions with witnesses. So if he's being taken to task for not giving an explanation, he should have the opportunity to give that explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps you can give the explanation now. If the municipal assembly thought it fit to take certain measures which in your opinion are in themselves a violation of the rules of the statute, why would they do so? Would it be because the ARK crisis was an institution which had no importance? Or was it because the ARK crisis actually was the institution which was important at the time? This is what was put to you by Ms. Korner, and you didn't agree with. And the two don't -- your statement and your explanation don't go together.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was put to me by the Prosecutor that I knew that it had authority, that it was a powerful organ. I beg to differ with this allegation. In particular, with the fact that I was aware of that. To clear this issue, first, as to why in this case one particular organ at the time -- in very chaotic times, why such an organ adopted a decision to this effect, I don't know. I couldn't tell you the reasons why this decision was adopted. Someone else could perhaps do that. I know that where dozens of other decisions adopted on a daily basis which were not subject to any consideration or any adequate decision-making process. I don't know whether I have managed to explain my position. I do not agree that it was a powerful body, a body that had authority, and I cannot explain the reasons why this was done in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was the only regional authority, wasn't it? The assembly first of all, and then the crisis staff. There was no other regional authority?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, in the instructions from Mr. Dzeric which you looked at yesterday, and you may want to have it back again - it's P --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It will be tab number 9 in his book.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know, but for the purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is it 157? I can't remember. I'm sorry, Your Honour, I thought I had brought it down today, but I seemed to have left it behind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, are you going to refer him to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am. P157, the last -- paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you got it there? "The crisis staff has convene, make decisions in the presence of its members, take official minutes" -- I take it as you told us yesterday, that although you can't remember it, minutes must have been taken. "Issue written decisions, submit weekly reports to the regional and state organisations." Do you remember reading that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have it here. I can have a look at it. Are you talking about paragraph 14? Yes, I have read it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you read it at the time, you told us.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand. What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll start this one again, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise really, but...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that although you deny ever seeing what we call variant A and B instructions, you did see in 1992 the instructions from Mr. Dzeric.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly when it was that I saw them, but I am familiar with them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. Did you see those instructions in April 1992, or early May?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is what I said. I believe I did, but 11 years down the road, I really cannot remember exactly. I believe that it worked according to these instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And paragraph 14 instructs you to deliver weekly reports to the regional authorities.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what you did, wasn't it, by somebody from the crisis staff attending the Monday meetings of the crisis staff of the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my assumption. I don't know for sure that reports were done and submitted to all of these addressees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And clearly, as we've discussed earlier, the prime minister of the Serbian government considered that the regional authorities was someone to whom the municipalities should report. You would agree with that, wouldn't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is why, sir, I suggest to you - let me come back to the same suggestion - you were following directions and orders from the regional crisis staff. And by "you," I mean your municipality, the SDS in your municipality.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still abide by what I testified before. In view of this statute and in view of the character of the association of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, we were not bound by their orders. We didn't have to implement them. And the reports were submitted on a regular basis. They were made in several copies and addressed to the relevant addressees, such as the state organs of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So to an organisation which existed at the time. It is clear that the Autonomous Region of Krajina existed at the time, but it does not mean that we had to abide by their decisions outside the statute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether you had to or not, the reality is for the important matters you did, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the form of that question because it doesn't specify what she means when she says "the important matters." So I object to the form.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to come to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, let's take disarmament of the Muslims. That came about, didn't it, with the deadlines as a result of instructions from the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regional crisis staff did adopt a decision to that effect with specified time limits. But I don't think that it said disarming of Muslims, but disarming of paramilitary formations. I remember that, and I know that units of the Territorial Defence were in charge of that, or the police. I don't remember exactly. So we were talking about disarming, disarmament. It was an interest that we had at the time and which had to be taken care of. I already explained to you that the situation was chaotic, and what my conduct was at the time. Each of us behaved as best as we could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, well you're absolutely right, sir. That's what the order actually said. It just said "paramilitaries." But in actual fact, in Bosanski Novi, as everywhere else, the only disarming that was done was of non-Serbs, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm that. I am not hundred per cent sure. I don't have any evidence to that effect. But it is possible that some Serbs were also disarmed. I do not have any specific information as to whose weapons specifically were seized at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were, weren't you, sir, heavily involved as you've already told us in the negotiations that went on with the Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I imagine you were shown by Mr. Cunningham the newspaper article to that effect. Could you hand back P1626.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Rather than having the usher look, we've got a spare copy here. Can that be handed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's an article in Glas on the 8th of May, and it describes those negotiations between yourself on behalf of the SDS and Muhamedagic on behalf of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can just give me a moment to have a look at the document, I have not seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't shown it by Mr. Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. With your permission, please, just a second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was in the folder yesterday, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I didn't use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was in the folder.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was amongst the documents that you had indicated to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember this? This was the meeting you were talking about yesterday in your evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had several meetings with Mr. Muhamedagic, and this was probably one of those, but I don't recall the exact venue and the time of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You, in fact, told us that you had been involved in negotiations in Bosanska Kostajnica, but you had also been involved in these negotiations in the actual Bosanski Novi itself, hadn't you? That's what this is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But I dedicated more time and more attention to Kostajnica. I was the president of the municipal SDS, and that was one of the topics that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you were the president of the municipal SDS of Bosanski Novi. Kostajnica was a tiny, tiny place, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We mentioned it yesterday. It was not such a tiny place. It had a population of 6500, compared to the 42.000-strong municipality, with a similar ethnic composition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And why was it you and not Mr. Pasic as the president of the municipal assembly who was engaged in these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ethnic tensions were already very high. And obviously, the SDS was representing the Serbian people at the time, and the SDA, the Muslim population. And the president of the assembly is someone who should have acted as some kind of mediator, not on behalf of any particular party. So that was one of the reasons why. We wanted to show that both SDS and SDA were appealing to those who were still illegally holding weapons to hand them over to the relevant authorities. So I attended the meeting on behalf of the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's just look at what the report says in the beginning. "Today in Bosanski Novi, days-long negotiations between the representatives of the SDS and the Party of Democratic Action on the implementation of the decisions of the Serbian Republic and the Autonomous Region Bosanska Krajina have successfully been brought to an end." Next sentence: "This primarily" - primarily - "regards the issue of disarming illegally armed groups and individuals who are not part of the regular municipal TO forces." Now, the majority of people who were not in the TO were the Bosniaks, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And although the decisions or the decision by the ARK Crisis Staff didn't say "Bosniaks," that's what was meant, wasn't it? And you knew that.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree, once again. There were regular units, the Territorial Defence, the police, and the military. We urged all those who held weapons and which were not -- who were not part of these structures to hand them in. We knew at the time that most Bosniaks were not in the TO. But if you look at the end of this article, it states clearly here that we both urged and we agreed that representatives or members of the Bosniak ethnicity should also join the Territorial Defence and the police in order for them to reflect the ethnic structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a trick, wasn't it, sir? It was to trick the Bosniaks --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not a trick. This was something that I advocated quite sincerely, and I have to say that I actually managed to implement it to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, because look what happened within days of this agreement. The special forces came down, didn't they, from Banja Luka? Special intervention squad sent by the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. A group of people came, and they stated that that's who they were. But I was not familiar with their chain of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you said there was this group, and you suggested these were paramilitaries and illegal formations. To the contrary, you knew full well, didn't you, sir, that this was an authorised police squad sent by Banja Luka CSB, didn't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I stated quite clearly in my previous answers that they stated that they were a police unit and that as far as I was concerned, they were a paramilitary formation. In view of the way in which they operated, I have to say that I was not aware of their chain of command. They did state that they were a police unit. But in view of the fact in which they operated, I considered them to be a paramilitary unit or a group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I absolutely agree with you, sir. But they were an authorised, legal paramilitary group, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Object to the question. It has already been answered. He said he didn't know where they came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He didn't know the chain of command. He has confirmed that at least twice, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, this constant American objection of asked and answered is simply not in my submission a proper one. It is perfectly proper to ask the same question even if an answer was given if there are other facts related.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Then I'll give another American objection. The continued questioning would be cumulative. It has been gone over before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The only problem that there is in this particular instance is that he has answered the question with regard to the chain of command already yesterday and today, and he has confirmed that he was not aware of the chain of command of this so-called paramilitary group, according to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see -- you were watching television at that time, were you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that I did not, but I did not spend a lot of time watching TV because I did not have the opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did, because that's what I usually do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the publicity given to the formation of the special intervention squad of the CSB either on television or in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not recall any details pertaining to these events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you attend the meeting, the assembly meeting, on the 12th of May 1992 in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th of May?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 12th of May 1992, when the creation -- when the VRS was created and the six strategic goals of the Serbian People were enumerated?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that on the 12th of May, that was the period when the tensions were high in the municipality and that I did not go there to attend the meeting. I do not remember that session, and I believe I did not attend it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know a gentleman named Mr. Vjestica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know him. Vjestica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the deputy for Bosanska Krupa?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which was a neighbouring municipality of yours?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that in Bosanska Krupa already by the 12th of May that there had been a total separation of the Bosniaks and the Serbs in that municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm looking now, please, at -- I'm looking at P50. And I'll give you the B/C/S if you want.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vjestica was giving a report to the assembly about conditions in Krupa and other municipalities on the Croatian border. And he said this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is page 26 of the translation. As I say, I'll bring it up if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "As for Bosanski Novi, let me tell you that I was there yesterday. Bosanski Novi is sealed off. An ultimatum has been issued, and a deadline set for the Muslims to surrender their weapons." Was that true?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on it. I was not there. And if you're asking me what Mr. Vjestica said, I cannot. But if you're asking me whether an ultimatum had been issued, there was a deadline for the surrender of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we take this in stages, I'm sorry. Split this up. First of all, do you agree as a matter of fact - forget about Mr. Vjestica seeing it - that Bosanski Novi had been sealed off?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the 11th of May?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 12th. Well, yes, it would have been the day before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Day before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sealed off by the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would use a Bosniak term for seal off. There was a police, and there was the army. But I do not really know what is meant by this term "seal off." The military and the police, they performed their own functions. But I don't know what you mean when you say "seal off" the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm using the words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you show him the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think the original should be in his own language, and he will be in a position --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have marked it up. I can show him the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You understand that I can't intervene on something like this and suggest questions or answers to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the purposes of the note, this is page 16 in the original Cyrillic, so I hope I've got the right place. And the part should be at page 17. Does Your Honour want to have the English on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, not really, Ms. Korner. And you, Mr. Cunningham, do you need it on the ELMO or on the corresponding --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm fine, Your Honour. Thank you but no thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've seen what the original says, sir. Do you understand what "sealed off" means?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blockaded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that was the situation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, I don't really know whether I have the right to answer this question at all. To say that a town is "sealed off," it means that nobody could go anywhere, and that was not what the situation was like. But if by saying "seal off," you mean to say that the military and the police set up certain checkpoints to carry out certain controls, to control a territory, then, yes, that was the situation. The word "to seal off" can be taken to mean two or three various things. If you are not happy with my answer, perhaps we can --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm suggesting to you that what had happened was that the army and the police were there in force, that blockades had been set up so that nobody could leave. And I'm asking you whether you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that they manned certain positions, but I believe that it was possible to pass through despite these positions if one wanted to go somewhere, one could do so. They took up certain positions in order to carry out checks, to check whether somebody was armed. Things like that. So the police and the military were present. They did take up certain positions. They did carry out checks trying to find weapons. But I do not believe that there was a total blockade imposed which would mean that nobody could go anywhere, neither in nor out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to the next part that Mr. Vjestica said to the assembly. "An ultimatum has been issued." You agree with that? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember now. All those who held weapons illegally were asked to hand them in by a certain date. There was a deadline imposed. I think that it was stated that if the weapons were not surrendered, the competent authorities would carry out searches. If this is what you mean when you say an ultimatum, then it was an ultimatum. There was no other ultimatum put forward by Mr. Vjestica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then the next part: "A deadline set for the Muslims to surrender their weapons." Why not the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say again that this deadline did not refer specifically to Muslims, but to all those who had illegal weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why Mr. Vjestica should be telling the assembly this was a deadline for Muslims only, and the same in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have no idea as to what Mr. Vjestica meant. What I'm saying is that as far as I'm concerned and as far as our activities in this town were concerned, our position was as I have just described it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, we're going to have a 25-minute break starting from now. And we'll continue soon after. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The usher, I suppose, is bringing in the witness. Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, if I may address the Court briefly, Mr. Pytlik, our intern, is with us today, and with your permission I would like for him to join us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Cunningham. And welcome again once more, because we have seen you before? Okay, thank you. The witness. Now, while we wait for the witness to come in, as we go along, Mr. Cunningham, and roughly in good time before the next break, please give us an indication how much you require for redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: As it stands right now, about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So that gives you an idea of how much time you have, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, as Mr. Cunningham has said, it's five minutes, I won't raise what otherwise I might raise. My cross-examination should not be limited by how much he wants --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, but I'm trying to get the witness out of The Hague today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He will be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If that is not possible, then obviously we will have to discuss other matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, he will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm working on that assumption, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. The reality of the situation around the 10th, 11th, 12th of May was that Bosanski Novi was full of units that fell under the 5th, later the 1st Krajina Corps, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They had complete control over the territory, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, thank you. You've negated the necessity to put to you a number of documents. Now, the intervention squad that came from Banja Luka, as you rightly told us yesterday, behaved exceedingly badly, didn't they? Can you have a look, please, at P1652. You told us yesterday that there had been a letter from the Bosanska Kostajnica police chief or station commander. Is that the letter you were thinking of?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify. This I said that I spoke to the chief of police, and that we were trying to find a solution as to how to get rid of these people. And as far as I know, he sent this letter and started the correspondence related to the attempts to solve this problem. I believe that this is the letter. In fact, when I look at it, I can confirm that this is the letter. I myself did not write it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But the only reason it was - a complaint was made, wasn't it - was because Serbs were complaining about the behaviour of these men?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not the only reason. It is a very important reason first of all. The Serbs did not complain about the way these people treated Serbs. Serbs did not agree with the actions of these men towards Muslims. That was one of the reasons. Another reason, I think that the local police commander stated, I think, four reasons, normative reasons for which he did not agree with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but what I'm putting to you, sir, is the only reason that the letter was ever sent was because local Serbs complained about the behaviour of these men, and I agree, towards Muslims; they didn't like what was being done.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that this is the only reason, because the commander stated some other reasons, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, I suggest, this was a group that came under the control of the CSB and came to Bosanski Novi at the request of the SJB in Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My objection is two-fold. I object to the form of the question because it's a compound question. And secondly, I think it's an attempt to reask the same question he did before as to where these individuals came from and whose command they were under. And I believe he's already said he didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you that it is a compound question, and that it should be divided into two. But I would allow the questions, both questions, to be put to the witness again because he is now being asked to answer them in the light of what is contained in this document P1652. So Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show you another document in a moment. But as a member -- as president of the SDS, as a member of the assembly and/or the crisis staff at this stage, you had close liaison, didn't you, with the police chief in Bosanska Kostajnica and also with the police chief in Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew both these men. I cannot now say how close the relations were, but I knew both of them personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And this disarmament operation was an important operation, wasn't it, for the purposes of Bosanski Novi Municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the issue of disarmament was an important one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And didn't it involve close liaison between the police, the army, and the political authorities, yourself and Mr. Pasic, in Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meant that everybody should do their job which was in their sphere of competence. And they should also all cooperate with each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you also have a look, please, at P1657. This is a letter, isn't it, written by the chief of the Bosanski Novi police station, Mr. Kutlija.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dated the 21st of May and addressed to the Banja Luka CSB to the command of the special purpose detachment to Ljubomir Ecim personally. Now, did you know Mr. Ecim in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never even met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who he is now?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it's a report on -- it's headed, isn't it, "report on the work and actions by a unit from the special purposes detachment in the area under the control of this SJB." "Following a deterioration in the security situation in the Bosanski Novi Municipality on the 11th of May 1992 when uncontrolled shooting erupted first in the town and then around the predominantly Muslim villages in the Japra Valley, the security service centre of Banja Luka dispatched a unit from the special purposes detachment under the command of Mirko Lukic and a military police unit under the command of Major Stupar as support on the 14th of May. "On the 15th of May, the leading team of the Bosanski Novi SJB, including police inspector Vaso Skondric, sent the special unit of the CSB an armoured fighting vehicle to search the Muslim part of Bosanska Kostajnica." And then there's a description of what we saw in the previous letter. Now, do you agree that these men that were described yesterday as criminals who called them policemen were, in fact, a CSB unit under the command of your local SJB?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you prepared to change your opinion now? I mean, this is basically what it amounts to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going a bit further after that, Your Honour. But that's what -- that's the first question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, let me remind you that I said that this was a unit that had come to Kostajnica and that they stated that they were the police. I also said that according to -- on the basis of how they acted, I considered them to be a paramilitary unit. This memo indicates likewise they were given instructions to act in accordance with the law, and you have three laws stated here. And since they were in violation of these laws, I considered them to be a paramilitary unit. That was my opinion, and I tried to formulate it in those terms. Perhaps I did not express myself quite clearly. They stated that they were a police unit; but on the basis of their actions, I considered them to be a paramilitary unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you said yesterday, page 46 of the LiveNote, was this: "They introduced themselves as police. By what they'd done later on, I think it's a criminal group. I don't believe it's real police." That's what you told us yesterday. Now, it is not only -- I'm sorry, perhaps I can -- at the risk of attracting an objection, repeat the question. Is it clear, isn't it, from this document, sir, that this was an authorised CSB unit actually acting under the command of your local police station?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite clear from this memo, but I still maintain that they acted in violation of the law, and that is why, as far as I'm concerned, they were a paramilitary unit. They violated the law and instructions they had been given. I don't know whether I've made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what I'm suggesting -- I agree with you. What I'm suggesting to you is you knew perfectly well at the time that this badly behaved group of criminals was not only part of the CSB, but also acting as a result of instructions from your police station. In other words, they had gone into operation, whatever they did after that, as a result of your local policemen -- sorry, chief. And you knew that, didn't you, at the time, sir? That's what I'm suggesting to you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know that. I see from this memo that it was made on the 21st of May 1992, which would mean -- I really didn't know who these people were. At that time, I was in Kostajnica. I was not in daily contact. There simply wasn't time to be in contact with all these people. When I realised what the men were doing, I responded. We asked for these people -- in fact, I realised that these people did not act in accordance with any laws, any regulations. And that is why myself and all the other people listed here responded. I did not know that they would arrive. I did not know who they were. As far as I was concerned and as far as the local people were concerned, these people -- these men were unknown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, I suggest to you that these -- this special group was the beginnings of a series of actions initiated to drive the Muslims out of Bosanski Novi. That's the reality, isn't it, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say what their task was, what their raison d'etre was. What I know is that we offered some kind of a resistance to them, and that we demanded that they do not act in the way that they had acted until then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because thereafter, as you told us yesterday, and I suggest to you that you used entirely the correct word, shelling and shooting of Muslim areas, particularly in the Japra Valley, began, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly when the problems in the Japra Valley began. You asked me what date it was, after which date. But I believe that the problems in Japra Valley erupted precisely around this period when the police unit came. I'm not quite sure, however.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an incident involving a military -- some military police at a checkpoint. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was then used as an excuse by units under the command of the 1st Krajina Corps, or the 5th as it still was then, to shell Muslim areas.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot state that there was shelling, and I cannot state that the shelling was carried out by units of the 1st Krajina Corps. It is true that this incident happened and that it caused problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people who lived in the Muslims areas of the Japra Valley were driven from their homes, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true that they left their homes and the problems that ensued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question wasn't -- I apologise to the interpreters for butting in like that. The question wasn't whether it's true that they left; the question is whether it's true that they had been driven out. Which is different. So please, answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that the term "driven out" was used. But I was not in the field, and I cannot state whether anyone went from house to house forcing them to leave. I know that they left their homes. I'm sure that they didn't do it voluntarily. They did it because they were afraid and for other reasons. They left their homes. But I cannot state that somebody went from house to house forcing them to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have -- are you telling us that you had absolutely no liaison on the crisis staff with the military forces in your area?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Territorial Defence staff, I think that he attended the sessions of the crisis staff. But I have to say that in Novi, just a few sessions of the crisis staff were held. I cannot recall any specific details. The commander of the Territorial Defence staff did attend the sessions of the crisis staff, but he was -- he had his place in the military chain of command, and he was accountable to them, to his superiors there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but nonetheless the military weren't operating in isolation, were they? You, the civilian authorities, had to know what was happening?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian authorities had the obligation to provide logistics support to the military. In any situations in which the military was activated. That is why it was necessary to coordinate things with the military forces. That was the reason why we were in communication. Of course, we were not blind. We all knew that there were problems in the field. We were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had to issue - and if you need to, I'll show you - you, the civilian authorities, had to issue orders that rubble from destroyed villages and areas were cleared away, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rubble in urban areas, this is what happened later. The rubble that was endangering the safety of civilians had to be removed, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had to be told, didn't you, something about the operations that were being carried out by the military, by the TO against Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that there were problems from the TO, from the police. We were informed by them that the paramilitary structures were causing problems. And I believe that we requested from the competent military and police bodies to put an end to the activities of the paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I am suggesting to you that this wasn't paramilitaries, as you told us yesterday, firing on villages; this was units of the regular army, plus the TO. And I'm equally suggesting to you that you know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with your suggestions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 1st -- I'm sorry. Yes, around the 1st of June, the town of Bosanski Novi was itself shelled, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember. I know that there were some incidents, but I cannot now recall the exact time and the events in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not incidents, sir; actual, organised, military, targeted shelling. That is what happened, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any organised, military shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been some individuals -- in fact, there were some individuals who were not under the control of the military organs, or paramilitary groups, which carried out some bad acts, so to speak. But they did it on their own -- of their own volition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us, and I'm sorry, I'm going to put the exact date to you, that on the 10th of June, the shelling that took place in the town of Bosanski Novi with long-range guns, if you like, was done by paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already stated in my previous answer that this may have been carried out by irresponsible individuals and paramilitary formations who did that without having been ordered to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember troops coming into the town of Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember what troops you're referring to. I said that Novi was a place where a lot of troops came and went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you be specific as regards the date, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 10th of June and thereafter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the houses of Muslims being set on fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never denied that there were incidents. I cannot really remember what you're referring to, but there were incidents in that time period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this was the central town in Bosanski Novi. Are you telling us that the army and the police stood by and let these rogue paramilitary units do this to the town?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think one could say that there were incidents, the military and the police at that time, in the chaos that reigned at the time, really did have problems controlling all the individuals and groups and that they were not able to control everything. All the paramilitary units and the irresponsible individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought we'd agreed some minutes ago that the troops under the control of the 1st Krajina Corps had complete control of the territory of Bosanski Novi at this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to apologise. I did not understand your question. You stressed the word "full control," which would mean the control over every corner, every house. There was no full control. This type of control did not exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So somehow or other, these rogue paramilitaries managed to get the hills around the town of Bosanski Novi, set up their weapons, start firing, move into the town, start burning houses, and nobody could stop them. That's what you're telling us, is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say that there were many sincere and strong attempts to put everything under control, but it was simply not possible to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And equally, I suggest, to your knowledge and with your acquiescence, the military moved all the Muslims out of the Japra Valley?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not with my acquiescence. I was informed about it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Hold it. At this point in time, I think I have to caution the witness. If at any time Ms. Korner puts any question to you which you prefer not to answer because, in your opinion, it might involve you in what happened or may have happened in the region and may expose you, then you can ask us, you can ask me, to be exempted from answering that question. And the Rules provide us with the authority to exempt you, as well as not to exempt you. But I don't think that will be the case. So if there are any questions that are put to you which may expose you to criminal proceedings, please, do intervene and ask us to be exempted from answering the question. I had avoided to do this until now because I didn't think the questions were anything which would really worry the witness. But I think at this stage I need to caution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this right: The Hotel Una, was that a private enterprise or owned by the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DEJANOVIC [Resumed]
